questions.question: Which two checkpoints in a tool invocation never produce a JSON-RPC message of their own?
options: Discover and list, since caching means they are skipped
Select and confirm, since both happen only inside the host
Call and result, since both are folded into a single round trip
Validate and execute, since both happen only on the server
questions.explanation: Select is the model choosing a tool and confirm is the host's own approval gate; neither one is a wire method, so neither can appear as a request or a response.

questions.question: A tools/call names a tool the server has never registered. Which response is correct for 2026-07-28?
options: An input_required result asking the client to supply a different tool name
A complete result with isError true, since the model can retry with a new name
A JSON-RPC error with code -32602, since the tool itself was never registered
A JSON-RPC error with code -32601, since the method itself is unknown
questions.explanation: The tools/call method was recognized fine; only the tool name inside it was invalid, which is Invalid params, -32602, not the -32601 reserved for an unrecognized method.

questions.question: publish_release is called with a missing required argument. Where does this fail and how is it reported?
options: At execute, as a JSON-RPC error with code -32603
At execute, as a complete result with isError set to true
At confirm, since the host should have caught it before sending the call
At validate, as a JSON-RPC error with code -32602
questions.explanation: Validate only confirms the tool is known; a missing or malformed argument is caught once execute checks the arguments against the tool's own schema, and it comes back as an actionable isError result.

questions.question: A client's request to get_build_status timed out. What is the resultType of the response that ends this call?
options: There is no such result: the caller simply stops waiting
"timed_out", a dedicated resultType the server returns for this case
"complete", with isError true and a message about the timeout
"cancelled", since the client gave up and tore down the request
questions.explanation: Neither a timeout nor a cancellation is a resultType; the server never gets to send a result the client still cares about, so the caller simply stops waiting and moves on.

questions.question: get_build_status is mid-poll when the stream breaks before any response arrives. What should the client do next?
options: Start a brand new build, since the original handle is now permanently invalid
Send a fresh id for the same handle, since idempotentHint marks it safe
Reuse the same JSON-RPC id, since the server is still processing that request
Wait indefinitely, since a broken stream always resumes once the connection recovers
questions.explanation: Nothing about this transport is resumable, so the lost request must be reissued with a new id; get_build_status is annotated idempotentHint true, which is what makes a blind reissue reasonable here.

questions.question: A publish_release call returns input_required, the client gathers the change ticket, and retries. What must that retry include?
options: The same JSON-RPC id, plus a fresh requestState the client generates itself
A new JSON-RPC id only, requestState is never sent back to the server
A new JSON-RPC id, together with inputResponses and the exact requestState echoed back
The same JSON-RPC id as the first attempt, so the server can match them
questions.explanation: A retry is an independent request: it needs its own new id, inputResponses keyed to match inputRequests, and requestState echoed back exactly as the server sent it, never invented or reused from a prior id.
